questions.answer: The vertical coordinate is displacement. At 6.0 s, the displacement is -4.0 m, so the object is 4.0 m on the negative side of the reference point.

option_feedback.A: This gives a velocity and uses the wrong unit. A displacement-time coordinate gives position relative to the reference point.
option_feedback.B: Correct. Negative displacement places the object on the chosen negative side of the reference point.
option_feedback.C: A single displacement coordinate does not give total distance travelled.
option_feedback.D: A single point cannot show that the displacement stayed constant for an interval.

questions.answer: The graph reports velocity directly. A horizontal line at -3.0 m s^-1 means a constant negative velocity, so the object moves steadily in the negative direction.

option_feedback.A: Stationary motion requires velocity zero. The graph is at -3.0 m s^-1, and it does not show position.
option_feedback.B: Correct. Both the size and direction of velocity remain constant.
option_feedback.C: The velocity is neither changing nor positive.
option_feedback.D: Velocity alone at this interval does not show the object's total displacement from its start.

questions.answer: Horizontal means the vertical quantity is constant. Constant displacement gives stationary motion, while constant non-zero velocity gives steady motion.

option_feedback.A: Graph Y is above zero, so it shows non-zero velocity rather than rest.
option_feedback.B: Graph X has constant displacement, so its object does not move.
option_feedback.C: Correct. The same line shape has different meanings because the vertical axes differ.
option_feedback.D: The meanings are reversed. A horizontal displacement line is stationary; a horizontal non-zero velocity line is steady motion.
